maya (Support): FYI customers in EU are seeing 503s and some 401s starting ~10:02 UTC. Looks correlated to region routing.
maya (Support): Example: client sent X-Client-Region: eu-west-1 but response shows X-Region-Routed: us-east-1 and auth failures.
maya (Support): Minimal repro curl from customer:
```bash
curl -v -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
ali (SRE): On it. Can someone dump gateway/failover logs? Suspect cross-zone fallback kicked in and header preservation lost.
sam (Infra): Pulling envoy logs now. Running: kubectl -n infra logs -l app=gateway -c envoy --since=20m | grep req_1934567899
sam (Infra): Quick hit in access logs: route switched to fallback cluster at 10:02:05 and upstream_host shows api-us-east-1.internal.
sam (Infra): Access log line (sanitized): "[10:02:06] req=1934567899 GET /v1/generate 503 upstream_host=api-us-east-1.internal x-client-region="
maya (Support): Customer pasted this in: "timestamp=2026-06-15T10:02:10Z req=1934567899 status=503 upstream=api-us-east-1.internal x-client-region=eu-west-1" — they observed retries and billing impact. :rotating_light:
kevin (Billing): Seeing a clear spike in token units for EU-origin traffic concurrent to this. Roughly +10-15% on a few accounts. We should consider temporary credits.
zhen (Eng): I rolled a routing change this morning to shorten fallback TTL to speed failover (09:45 UTC). That would cause more aggressive cross-zone routing. TTL was 120s -> 30s.
ali (SRE): TTL change explains faster switching. But header truncation suggests host-rewrite or header_filter behavior in Envoy when routing to fallback cluster. I'll inspect route-level header manipulations.
sam (Infra): Confirmed: we have a route-level host rewrite that rewrites :authority when proxying to east pool and the current config does not preserve X-Client-Region. Looks like header is dropped during host rewrite.
sam (Infra): Snippet from route config (relevant bits): 
```
route: { cluster: api-us-east-1, host_rewrite: api-us-east-1.internal, request_headers_to_remove: ["X-Client-Region"] }
```
ali (SRE): That request_headers_to_remove is the smoking gun. Who pushed that?
zhen (Eng): I didn't touch header removal; my change only modified fallback-ttl, not header list. Maybe another config change went in. I'll search git diff.
sam (Infra): Immediate mitigation options: revert fallback-ttl, remove header removal rule, or disable cross-zone fallback for eu-west-1. We can do both quick.
kevin (Billing): Sales wants us to proactively credit affected customers. I need the timeframe windows.
maya (Support): I'll collect affected account IDs as we confirm. Please provide the time range once metrics settle.
zhen (Eng): Rolling back fallback-ttl now (apply -f configs/routing/fallback-ttl.yaml -> 120s). Triggering rollout.
deploy-bot: [ci] started rollout: routing-config rollback -> gateway by zhen at 2026-06-15T10:04:12Z
sam (Infra): Patching envoy config to stop removing X-Client-Region on host rewrite. Applying patch to configmap envoy-route.
sam (Infra): Command: kubectl patch configmap envoy-route -n infra --patch 'replace request_headers_to_remove with []' (applied)
ali (SRE): I'll add an alert that fires if auth failure rate for region eu-west-1 > 1% above baseline and cross-zone routing > 2% of requests.
kevin (Billing): Please tag all affected accounts so we can queue credits. I can approve a temporary one-off credit policy for confirmed errors.
maya (Support): Noted. I'll open a billing ticket with list. Also will send a short customer-facing update: rollback + header fix in progress, ETA 10-15m.
zhen (Eng): Rollback completed at 10:05:02Z per CI.
sam (Infra): Envoy config change deployed at 10:06:30Z. Observability shows X-Client-Region preserved in new access logs and fewer 401s.
ali (SRE): Auth failures and 5xxs trending down over next 5m. Still monitoring for stragglers.
maya (Support): Customers confirming recovery around 10:09 UTC. They requested a postmortem and compensation.
sam (Infra): I'm creating an incident ticket (INC-2026-042): include timeline, root cause (header removed during host rewrite + aggressive fallback TTL), mitigation, and billing impact. ETA for postmortem doc: 24 hours.
kevin (Billing): Thanks. Please include a proposed credit formula in the postmortem (tokens spent on retries + fixed goodwill credit).
maya (Support): Will do. Closing notes: follow-up actions assigned: (1) audit all header removal rules before rollouts, (2) gating fallback-ttl changes behind canary, (3) add unit test for header preservation on host rewrite.
ali (SRE): Agreed. I'll own the monitoring and the alerting adjustments.
maya (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll update customers with incident ticket and planned credits. :thumbsup:
